root_cause.text: The ublk block-device partition scan worker dereferenced `ub->ub_disk` without holding a reference, so concurrent device teardown could NULL out and free the `gendisk` before `ublk_partition_scan_work()` used it, causing a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces direct `ub->ub_disk` access in `ublk_partition_scan_work()` with `ublk_get_disk()`/`ublk_put_disk()` to pin the `gendisk`, and the commit message explicitly states the race: `ublk_stop_dev_unlocked()` does `del_gendisk()`, `ublk_detach_disk()` sets `ub->ub_disk = NULL`, `put_disk()` may free it, after which the worker dereferences `ub->ub_disk`; it also changes `flush_work()` to `cancel_work_sync()` to avoid running the work after detach.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch replaces direct `ub->ub_disk` access in `ublk_partition_scan_work()` with `ublk_get_disk()`/`ublk_put_disk()` to pin the `gendisk`, and the commit message explicitly states the race: `ublk_stop_dev_unlocked()` does `del_gendisk()`, `ublk_detach_disk()` sets `ub->ub_disk = NULL`, `put_disk()` may free it, after which the worker dereferences `ub->ub_disk`; it also changes `flush_work()` to `cancel_work_sync()` to avoid running the work after detach.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the partition-scan work helper that triggered disk change notification and partition rescanning from this code path.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the entire static function `ublk_partition_scan_work(struct work_struct *work)`, which previously derived `struct ublk_device *ub` from `work`, checked and cleared `GD_SUPPRESS_PART_SCAN` with `test_and_clear_bit()`, and if successful locked `ub->ub_disk->open_mutex`, called `bdev_disk_changed(ub->ub_disk, false)`, then unlocked the mutex.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code no longer schedules or performs this partition-scan work path from this location, so the associated disk-change notification and partition rescan trigger are no longer executed here. This removes the suppression-bit check and the mutex-protected `bdev_disk_changed()` call that would have notified the block layer of a changed disk state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a safe deferred partition-scan work item for ublk disks to rescan partitions without risking teardown races.
intent_record.what: A new workqueue callback function, `ublk_partition_scan_work()`, was added. It retrieves the enclosing `ublk_device`, obtains a reference to the associated `gendisk` via `ublk_get_disk()`, checks and clears `GD_SUPPRESS_PART_SCAN` with `test_and_clear_bit()`, locks `disk->open_mutex`, calls `bdev_disk_changed(disk, false)`, then unlocks and drops the disk reference with `ublk_put_disk()`. The function also includes a `WARN_ON_ONCE()` if the suppress-partition-scan flag was not set.
intent_record.how: This enables deferred partition rescanning for the ublk disk while protecting against use-after-free during teardown by holding a disk reference. At runtime, it triggers a disk change notification only once after the suppress flag is cleared, causing the block layer to re-evaluate partitions safely under the disk open mutex.

intent_record.intent_summary: Make ublk device shutdown safely cancel pending partition scan work before teardown continues.
intent_record.what: In ublk_stop_dev(), the call to flush_work(&ub->partition_scan_work) was replaced with cancel_work_sync(&ub->partition_scan_work) before ublk_cancel_dev(ub) is called.
intent_record.how: This changes the shutdown path so any pending partition scan work is not only flushed but also synchronously cancelled if it is queued or running, ensuring the work item cannot execute after device teardown proceeds.

grouping_result.intent: Remove the partition-scan work helper that triggered disk change notification and partition rescanning from this code path.
Make ublk device shutdown safely cancel pending partition scan work before teardown continues.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure ublk disk teardown is safe by managing deferred partition scan work to avoid races during shutdown.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is a use-after-free in the ublk partition scan worker caused by dereferencing ub->ub_disk during teardown. Removing the partition-scan work helper directly addresses that code path and prevents the unsafe access.

The changes directly target the reported race in ublk partition scan work by adding safer deferred scan handling and cancelling pending scan work during teardown, which addresses the use-after-free caused by dereferencing ub->ub_disk without a valid reference.

This is the direct dereference of ub->ub_disk->state in the partition-scan worker; if teardown NULLs or frees ub->ub_disk concurrently, this access becomes a use-after-free.

Implement async partition scan to avoid IO hang when reading partition
tables. Simila
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 7fc4da6a304bdcd3de14fc946dc2c19437a9cc5a
Author: Ming Lei <ming.lei@redhat.com>
Date:   Tue Dec 23 11:27:40 2025 +0800

    ublk: scan partition in async way
    
    Implement async partition scan to avoid IO hang when reading partition
    tables. Similar to nvme_partition_scan_work(), partition scanning is
    deferred to a work queue to prevent deadlocks.
    
    When partition scan happens synchronously during add_disk(), IO errors
    can cause the partition scan to wait while hold
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the async scan worker dereferencing the disk pointer directly: `test_and_clear_bit(GD_SUPPRESS_PART_SCAN, &ub->ub_disk->state)` and `mutex_lock(&ub->ub_disk->open_mutex); bdev_disk_changed(ub->ub_disk, false);`. There is no reference acquisition or lifetime protection for `ub->ub_disk` in `ublk_partition_scan_work()`, so if teardown can NULL/free the gendisk before the work runs, this is the vulnerable use-after-free pattern described. The later `flush_work(&ub->partition_scan_work);` in `ublk_stop_dev()` helps stop pending work during device shutdown, but it does not add a ref or otherwise protect `ub->ub_disk` inside the worker itself, so the fix for the UAF is not present here.
